title: Stream session handshake proxy and FunctionCall compatibility shim
creator: Marco Li
description: Problem: Clients using legacy EventStream/SSE variants and middleboxes cause session resets, truncated function call payloads, and incompatible chunk framing. We need a deployable proxy/handshake layer that normalizes incoming connections to our canonical SSE eventstream framing and negotiates a resume token handshake, while simultaneously providing a compatibility shim so older client function-calling semantics (pre-structured output wire formats) map to our current FunctionCall envelope without changing user code. Goals: 1) Restore continuity for interrupted streams with a lightweight resume handshake. 2) Translate legacy function-call fragments into the structured FunctionCall JSON envelope server-side. 3) Provide backpressure hints and pacing to avoid overloading older clients or proxies. Constraints: minimal latency impact for normal requests (<5ms median overhead), no client SDK updates required, graceful rollback plan for runtime-1.20 rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy performs handshake and negotiates resume tokens for 99.9% of test cases under simulated middlebox resets
Legacy function-call fragments are reconstructed and emitted as a single structured FunctionCall event to downstream runtime with correct arguments and call id mapping
Added round-trip overhead introduced by the proxy is <10ms P50 and <25ms P95 in our benchmarks
Compatibility shim covered by automated e2e test suite including chunk loss, reordering, and duplicate chunk injection
Canary rollout config and automatic fallback to direct routing when proxy health < 99%
notes: Design doc: outlined a two-phase handshake: SYN(to proxy)->SYN-ACK(include resume token)->ACK(client). Resume token derived from sequence window metadata and per-session HMAC.
We considered client SDK updates but rejected because many enterprise customers cannot push upgrades quickly; server-side shim preferred.
Security: resume token lifecycle limited to 24h; tokens rotate on model version changes to avoid cross-version replays.
Telemetry: emit events for handshake failures, reconstructed function calls, and chunk repair rate to console rollup dashboards.
